source: YouTube auto-caption transcript 0:00-18:35 (tools/video_draft.py transcript 5aMQKjCukTc --start 0 --end 1115), card names corrected against data/Sets/FRA_PremierDraft_All_Data.json; nothing past the start of game 1 (about 18:29) read. 'type' marks each idea as claim, heuristic or one-off pick; 'repeats' lists ideas of earlier videos it restates (none); 'related' lists looser matches on the same card or topic.

ideas.claim: Draconic Visitor is overrated: mostly a big flier that dies to everything and hard to turn into the dragon; No Admittance is taken over it in a weak pack.
ideas.quote: Visitor is very mid. I think this is probably one of the most overrated cards in the sets.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR and ALSA of Draconic Visitor against other rares and No Admittance, skill-split.

ideas.claim: Recursive Recruitment is a very strong card; at P1p2 it is an easy pick over Master of Barbs and Geist of Saint Thalia.
ideas.quote: I think it's a pretty easy recursive recruitment here. This card is just excellent.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Recursive Recruitment in decks where it is main colour vs splash, skill-split.

ideas.claim: Read the first-pick neighbour: compare what the first pack lost against what it held, and move out of the colour that went. He sees red taken from the pack and moves toward blue-white / non-red.
ideas.quote: what did they take based on what was in the pack.
ideas.test_idea: Does the colour a first-pick pack loses predict which colours flow from that direction in pack 1? Needs the first-pack contents per draft (17Lands has no per-pack picks for other seats).

ideas.claim: A weak pack gives a removal spell off the plan (Vraska's Final Mercy) over playables for the plan.
ideas.quote: I guess there is this Frasis File Mercy. That's not junk.
ideas.test_idea: ALSA and GIH WR of Vraska's Final Mercy against the other cards in that pack; share of drafters who end black.

ideas.claim: Thalia, the Survivor is only fine: a three-mana 3/4 that taxes noncreature spells; not worth a high pick and cut from the final deck.
ideas.quote: don't love Thalia.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Thalia, the Survivor in white decks, skill-split.

ideas.claim: Generous Revival belongs to a black-white deck rather than blue-white, while Tam's Resistance is the blue-white card.
ideas.quote: Generous revival, I think, is more of an Obson card than a blue white card.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Generous Revival by colour pair: WB against WU.

ideas.claim: Blessed Ghoul is good with Empower Jace and surveil: a cheap one-drop that pumps when going wide and returns from the graveyard.
ideas.quote: Oh, ghoul comes back. Hell yeah. I mean it's kind of good with empower Jace and just surveilling.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Blessed Ghoul with the count of surveil / Empower Jace cards in the deck.

ideas.claim: A Jace blue-white deck needs creatures, ideally ones that can attack; Theorist's Proxy is taken over Fatehold Chronologist as the stronger card on theme.
ideas.quote: one thing with this deck is we do be needing creatures. Ideally, creatures that can attack.
ideas.test_idea: Creature count of winning UW Jace decks; GIH WR of Proxy against Chronologist.

ideas.claim: Take the two-drop the curve needs over the stronger Hexhaven Battalion: Enlightened Confidant over Battalion because the deck needs twos (Battalion is good with Kindred Judgment: it reaches seven mana and keeps creatures after the sweeper).
ideas.quote: I think enlightening Conan's good and I think I'm going to take it over battalion just because we need twos.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of decks by number of two-drops at the time of the pick; GIH WR of both cards.

ideas.claim: Generous Revival is a good card to take with surveil in the deck: a great thing to bring back, and surveil can fill the graveyard for it.
ideas.quote: now I'm a little more interested in general survival. Like this is a great thing to bring back.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Generous Revival against the number of surveil / self-mill cards in the deck.

ideas.claim: A second Blessed Ghoul is never wanted; he would spec on a land (Transformative Commons) or an off-colour card instead.
ideas.quote: I haven't really found I want second ghoul basically ever.
ideas.test_idea: Marginal value of a second Blessed Ghoul in the deck: win rate of decks with 2 against 1.

ideas.claim: Tetsuko Umezawa is a deck-dependent card: mediocre in a deck without the support, really good in the right one.
ideas.quote: Like she's right in that sweet spot of not great in every deck.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Tetsuko Umezawa, Fugitive split by the number of Empower Jace / counter cards in the deck.

ideas.claim: Prudent Fateseer is better than its 17Lands numbers say; he rates it highly despite the stats.
ideas.quote: This card doesn't have great stats on 17 lands, but I I really really like this card a lot.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck GIH WR of Prudent Fateseer by skill group; compare with its raw GIH WR.

ideas.claim: Take the Jace land (Theorist's Sanctum) over Saheeli, Consul of Oversight; Saheeli is good if triggered the turn she comes down and wheels at pick 10.
ideas.quote: I love Sanctum too. There's Sahili. Uh, she is quite good as long as you can trigger her the turn she comes down.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Saheeli with the number of instants/sorceries or wizards in the deck; wheel rate of Saheeli.

ideas.claim: Fblthp, Impossibly Lost is better than he had it ranked: he was a little too low on it after a Discord comment on his last episode and playing it a lot this week.
ideas.quote: I was a little too low on it.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR and IWD of Fblthp, Impossibly Lost by skill group.

ideas.claim: With few removal spells, take the removal (Surgical Precision) over the strong creature (Fblthp); with two more removal spells he would take the creature.
ideas.quote: If I had like two more removal spells, I would vote the other way.
ideas.test_idea: Value of the Nth removal spell: marginal win rate by removal count already in the pool at pick time.

ideas.claim: With Jace in the deck, curve is the tiebreaker: take the cheaper creature so a two goes into a three to protect the planeswalker (Theorix Metamage over Blossom-Blessed Angel).
ideas.quote: Especially when I have Jace, like when I've got Jace, you really want to play a two into a three so you can protect it.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of Jace decks by number of two- and three-drops; GIH WR of the two cards.

ideas.claim: Sphinx's Approach is playable ('I don't hate it'), a late pick that makes his deck but is awkward to cast.
ideas.quote: I guess I don't hate this card.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Sphinx's Approach in blue decks, skill-split.

ideas.claim: A splash card is found late: Recursive Recruitment is splashed in a blue-white deck because the pool holds two white-black duals (Meticulous Commons x2).
ideas.quote: I didn't consider this during the draft, but maybe we're supposed to splash recruitment as well.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Recursive Recruitment as a splash card with 0, 1, 2 duals of its colour.

ideas.claim: When cutting, do not cut a two-mana card; cut the expensive or off-plan cards (Generous Revival, Tam's Resistance, Thalia, Sphinx's Approach).
ideas.quote: Although again, I don't really want to cut a two mana card.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of decks by cheap-card count when cutting from 41-42 playables.

ideas.claim: Aggressive decks are better right now: in his last ten or so drafts the midrange mirrors came down to who drew better.
ideas.quote: I've actually been leaning a little more aggressive in my past 10ish drafts.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate by archetype speed (average mana value) on 17Lands data, mirror matches against others.

ideas.claim: Never go below 17 lands: missing land drops is the worse failure; fill the extra slots with card draw instead.
ideas.quote: I never want to miss my land drops.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of 16 against 17 lands by deck archetype and by splash; test the claim that 17 beats 16 with a splash.

ideas.claim: Cut Sphinx's Approach for being awkward to cast when there is card advantage elsewhere, then keeps it at the end for the curve: 'slightly awkward mana be damned'.
ideas.quote: I think I can cut Spinx's approach. It's just like not going to be super easy to cast.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of decks containing Sphinx's Approach by number of its colour sources.

ideas.claim: Keep at least 13 creatures (counting the Recursive Recruitment tokens) when the deck has Jace and a team pump spell.
ideas.quote: My creature count is 13 plus recruitment, right? Don't think I want to go too much lower than that when I've got like a Jace and like a team pump spell.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of UW Jace decks by creature count (12-16).

ideas.claim: The math always points to 17 lands over 16, especially with a splash, both for hitting land drops and for source counts.
ideas.quote: the math always kind of points towards you playing 17 rather than 16 in in especially if you're splashing, right?
ideas.test_idea: Probability of hitting land drops and colour sources at 16 against 17 lands (hypergeometric), plus 17Lands win rate by land count with a splash.

ideas.claim: If you get flooded often, the fix is not cutting lands but adding things to do with your mana (card draw, sinks).
ideas.quote: the solve for that isn't cut lands. It's include more things to do with your mana.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate by number of mana sinks / card-draw cards at 17 lands.
